rule: Plain English name; avoid acronyms and jargon
format: Plain English, up to about 100 characters

rule: A short name to keep titles concise
Describes the data; usage warnings go elsewhere
example: Monthly counts of outpatient attendances by provider and specialty.

rule: Your own system's identifier or an opaque random one
format: Your system's identifier, or a random UUID

rule: The organisation that created the data
format: Link to an organisation in a published list
ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) or date and time

rule: The period the data applies to
format: ISO 8601 start and end dates, written start/end

rule: The standard or schema the data follows
format: Link to the standard or schema
example: A link to the NHS data set specification the extract follows

rule: open, commercial or internal, with any handling caveat
OGL URL for open data; the agreement for restricted data
format: Link to the licence or agreement

rule: How long this version is valid
The newer version that replaces this one
format: Link to the record that replaces this one
example: A link to the 2026 version's catalogue record
